sections.body: Course design and teaching with AI is the practical use of machine learning and language models to plan a course, write test questions, adjust material to a student, answer subject questions, and turn raw notes into usable lecture content. Right now, systems do not design whole degrees on their own. Instead, they work as assistants that compare a syllabus against a list of learning goals, generate draft quiz items from a textbook chapter, or rewrite a dense slide deck into simpler language. Some tools build a short practice test from a set of lecture notes, while others check whether an exam question actually matches the skill it is meant to measure. The work is narrow and task based, not a replacement for a teacher's judgment.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of this work is uneven. Generating a first draft of a multiple choice question or a lesson summary is now reliable enough to save time, but the output still needs a human check for factual errors and bias. Personalised learning systems can spot a student who is falling behind by looking at quiz scores and login patterns, yet they often cannot explain why the student is struggling or what to do about it beyond flagging the problem. Course-specific tutors can answer common questions about a single subject when they are given the right source material, but they still invent plausible wrong answers when asked something outside that material. Lecture material tools can turn notes into slides or outlines, but they do not yet understand what a particular class already knows. The honest limit is that these systems assist with preparation and monitoring, not with the actual teaching relationship.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to see how a syllabus is checked against stated goals should start with Curriculum and Learning Outcomes, which covers the mapping work. Generating Assessments shows what current tools can and cannot do when writing exam questions, rubrics, and practice tasks. Personalised Learning and Early Warning explains the systems that track student progress and flag risk, along with their limits. Course-Specific AI Tutors looks at assistants built for one subject or one course, where the source material is controlled. Lecture Materials from Notes covers the conversion of raw notes into slides, summaries, and study guides. Together these pages move from planning a course, to testing it, to supporting individual students, to producing the materials used in class.
